name: Central Park
short_description: 843 acres of meadows, lakes and winding paths through the middle of Manhattan, with the Ramble and Bethesda Terrace at its heart.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
address: Upper East Side, New York, NY
short_description: Two million works spanning five thousand years, from Egyptian temples to the rooftop garden overlooking Central Park.

name: Museum of Modern Art
short_description: Starry Night, Campbell's Soup Cans and a sculpture garden, arranged across six floors of modern and contemporary work.

name: American Museum of Natural History
address: Upper West Side, New York, NY
short_description: Blue whale overhead, dinosaur halls upstairs and the Rose Center planetarium next door. Built for wandering.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
address: Upper East Side, New York, NY
short_description: Frank Lloyd Wright's white spiral on Fifth Avenue. Take the lift up and walk the ramp down past the exhibitions.

name: Whitney Museum of American Art
short_description: American art from 1900 onward in a Renzo Piano building, with outdoor terraces looking over the High Line and the Hudson.

name: Tenement Museum
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY
short_description: Guided tours through restored apartments at 97 Orchard Street, telling the stories of the immigrant families who lived in them.

name: 9/11 Memorial Museum
short_description: The twin reflecting pools sit in the tower footprints, with the museum below ground holding the slurry wall and the last column.

name: Intrepid Museum
short_description: An aircraft carrier moored on the Hudson, carrying a flight deck of jets, the Concorde and the shuttle Enterprise.

name: The Met Cloisters
address: Fort Tryon Park, New York, NY
short_description: Medieval European art in a hilltop building assembled from French cloisters, with herb gardens above the Hudson.

name: The High Line
short_description: A mile and a half of disused freight line replanted as an elevated walkway from Gansevoort Street to Hudson Yards.

name: Bryant Park
short_description: A formal lawn behind the public library, with a carousel, free chairs everywhere and an ice rink through the winter.

name: Washington Square Park
short_description: The marble arch, the fountain and a permanent circle of chess players, buskers and NYU students in Greenwich Village.

name: Riverside Park
address: Upper West Side, New York, NY
short_description: Four miles of waterfront park along the Hudson, with the 79th Street boat basin and a promenade under the plane trees.

name: Little Island
short_description: A public park raised on tulip-shaped concrete piles over the Hudson, with an amphitheatre and layered planting.

name: The Battery
short_description: The southern tip of Manhattan, with harbour views to Liberty Island, Castle Clinton and the SeaGlass carousel.

name: Madison Square Park
short_description: A small Flatiron green with rotating outdoor sculpture commissions and the original Shake Shack in the corner.

name: Fort Tryon Park
short_description: Terraced paths and one of the best Hudson views in the city, wrapped around the Cloisters at Manhattan's northern end.

name: Empire State Building
short_description: The 1931 Art Deco tower, with observatories on the 86th and 102nd floors and a restored ceiling in the lobby.

name: Top of the Rock
short_description: The Rockefeller Center observation deck, and the one place you can photograph the Empire State Building in the skyline.

name: One World Observatory
short_description: Floors 100 to 102 of One World Trade Center, reached by a lift that animates four centuries of the city on the way up.

name: Edge
short_description: A triangular sky deck jutting out from Hudson Yards, with angled glass walls and a glass floor panel to stand on.

name: SUMMIT One Vanderbilt
short_description: Mirrored rooms, a reflective floor and glass ledges cantilevered over Madison Avenue, next to Grand Central.

name: Flatiron Building
short_description: The 1902 wedge at the junction of Broadway and Fifth, still one of the most photographed corners in the city.

name: Grand Central Terminal
short_description: The Beaux-Arts main concourse, its green astronomical ceiling, the whispering gallery and a lower-level dining hall.

name: Rockefeller Center
short_description: A complex of Art Deco towers around a sunken plaza that holds the skating rink and the Christmas tree.

name: Times Square
short_description: The crossroads of Broadway and Seventh, lit around the clock by billboards. Loud, crowded and unmistakably New York.

name: Statue of Liberty
short_description: Bartholdi's copper figure on Liberty Island, reached by ferry from the Battery, with pedestal and crown tickets sold separately.

name: Chinatown
short_description: Dense blocks of markets, bakeries and dumpling shops around Mott and Canal, with Columbus Park busy from early morning.

name: Harlem
short_description: Brownstone streets, gospel Sundays and a long musical history around 125th Street and Marcus Garvey Park.

name: Greenwich Village
short_description: Low brick townhouses on crooked streets, jazz basements and the cafes around Bleecker and MacDougal.

name: SoHo
short_description: The largest concentration of cast-iron architecture anywhere, with flagship shops filling the ground floors.

name: Lower East Side
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY
short_description: Tenement blocks turned over to galleries, record shops, bars and the old appetizing stores that stayed put.

name: Little Italy
short_description: A few surviving blocks of Mulberry Street, with pastry counters, red-sauce restaurants and the San Gennaro feast.

name: Chelsea Market
short_description: A food hall in the old Nabisco factory where the Oreo was invented, opening straight onto the High Line.

name: Essex Market
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY
short_description: A public market trading since 1940, now in a new hall on Delancey with produce, fishmongers and prepared food upstairs.

name: Union Square Greenmarket
short_description: Regional farmers fill the north end of Union Square four days a week, year round, whatever the weather.

name: The Drawing Center
short_description: The only museum in the country devoted to drawing, showing historical and contemporary work in a SoHo loft.

name: Apollo Theater
short_description: The Harlem stage where Amateur Night launched Ella Fitzgerald and James Brown, still running weekly.

name: Broadway Theater District
short_description: Forty-one theatres in the blocks around Times Square, with the TKTS steps selling same-day seats at a discount.

name: Lincoln Center
short_description: A campus for the Metropolitan Opera, the Philharmonic and City Ballet, arranged around a travertine plaza and fountain.

name: Radio City Music Hall
short_description: A 1932 Art Deco hall with the largest proscenium in the world, home to the Rockettes and their Christmas show.

name: Carnegie Hall
short_description: The 1891 concert hall on 57th Street whose main auditorium is still considered among the finest anywhere for sound.

name: Blue Note Jazz Club
short_description: A small Greenwich Village room booking major jazz names two sets a night, with tables tight against the stage.

name: Pier 17
short_description: A rebuilt Seaport pier with a rooftop concert lawn looking straight at the Brooklyn Bridge and the East River.

name: Hudson River Park
short_description: Four miles of piers, lawns and bike path along the west side, running from the Battery up to 59th Street.

name: East River Esplanade
address: Upper East Side, New York, NY
short_description: A quiet waterfront walk on the Upper East Side, looking across to Roosevelt Island and the Queensboro Bridge.

name: South Street Seaport
short_description: Cobbled streets and nineteenth-century counting houses beside the East River, with historic ships tied up at the pier.

name: Conservatory Garden
short_description: Central Park's only formal garden, six acres in Italian, French and English styles, entered through the Vanderbilt Gate.

name: Jefferson Market Garden
short_description: A volunteer-run garden on the site of a former jail, beside the Victorian Gothic Jefferson Market Library.

name: Heather Garden
address: Fort Tryon Park, New York, NY
short_description: Three acres of heath and perennial planting on a ridge in Fort Tryon Park, with the Hudson and the Palisades below.

name: Federal Hall
short_description: Where Washington took the first presidential oath, marked by his statue on the steps opposite the Stock Exchange.

name: Hamilton Grange
short_description: Alexander Hamilton's country house, moved twice and restored in St Nicholas Park with its original room plan.

name: Morris-Jumel Mansion
short_description: Manhattan's oldest surviving house, built 1765, used by Washington as a headquarters during the battle for New York.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
short_description: The 1883 granite-and-steel crossing to Brooklyn, with a raised pedestrian promenade running down the centre of the span.

name: Manhattan Bridge
short_description: The quieter East River crossing, with a walkway that gives the classic view back at the Brooklyn Bridge.

name: Madison Square Garden
short_description: The arena above Penn Station, home to the Knicks and the Rangers and a constant concert schedule.

name: Chelsea Piers
short_description: A sports complex built into four Hudson River piers, with golf, climbing, skating and batting cages.

name: Circle Line Sightseeing Cruises
short_description: Sightseeing boats from Pier 83 that run the full loop around Manhattan, narrated, in about two and a half hours.

name: Roosevelt Island Tramway
address: Upper East Side, New York, NY
short_description: A commuter cable car over the East River that costs a subway fare and gives an unmatched midtown view.

name: Brooklyn Museum
short_description: A vast collection strong in Egyptian art and American painting, with the Sackler Center's Dinner Party on permanent show.

name: New York Transit Museum
short_description: Housed in a decommissioned 1936 subway station, with a platform of vintage cars you can walk through.

name: Brooklyn Children's Museum
short_description: The first museum built for children anywhere, opened 1899, with hands on exhibits across a green-roofed building.

name: The City Reliquary
short_description: A tiny volunteer museum of New York ephemera: subway tokens, seltzer bottles, Statue of Liberty souvenirs.

name: Prospect Park
short_description: Olmsted and Vaux's second park, with the Long Meadow, a ravine of old-growth forest and the city's only lake.

name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
short_description: Eighty-five acres along the East River piers, with Jane's Carousel and the best skyline view in the city at dusk.

name: McCarren Park
short_description: The open green between Williamsburg and Greenpoint, with a running track, ball fields and a 1936 pool.

name: Fort Greene Park
short_description: A hilltop park by Olmsted and Vaux, crowned by the Prison Ship Martyrs Monument and its granite stairs.

name: Sunset Park
short_description: The park the neighborhood is named for, with a view across the harbour taking in both the skyline and the Statue of Liberty.

name: Marine Park
short_description: Brooklyn's largest park, wrapped around a salt marsh with a boardwalk trail through the grasses and tidal creek.

name: Domino Park
short_description: Built on the old Domino Sugar refinery site, keeping the syrup tanks and cranes as structure along the waterfront.

name: Bushwick Inlet Park
short_description: A green waterfront strip on the Greenpoint side of the inlet, looking straight across at midtown Manhattan.

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
short_description: Fifty-two acres including a Japanese hill-and-pond garden and the cherry esplanade that draws crowds each spring.

name: Narrows Botanical Gardens
short_description: A volunteer-built garden along the Bay Ridge shore, with a native plant meadow and views of the Verrazzano.

name: 6/15 Green Community Garden
short_description: A small Park Slope community garden run by neighbours, open on weekends and planted for pollinators.

name: Green-Wood Cemetery
short_description: 478 acres of Victorian funerary landscape on Brooklyn's highest hill, with monk parakeets nesting in the gatehouse.

name: Old Stone House
short_description: A reconstructed Dutch farmhouse marking the Battle of Brooklyn, now a small museum inside Washington Park.

name: Weeksville Heritage Center
short_description: Four surviving houses of one of the first free Black communities in the country, preserved on their original lane.

name: Wyckoff House Museum
short_description: The oldest building in New York City, a Dutch saltbox dating to about 1652, with a working kitchen garden.

name: Brooklyn Heights Promenade
short_description: A cantilevered walkway over the BQE, giving an uninterrupted view of Lower Manhattan and the harbour.

name: The William Vale Rooftop
short_description: A Williamsburg hotel roof twenty-two floors up, with a wraparound terrace facing the Manhattan skyline.

name: Time Out Market Rooftop
short_description: The top floor of the DUMBO food hall, opening onto a terrace between the Brooklyn and Manhattan bridges.

name: DUMBO
short_description: Cobbled streets under the bridge approaches, with the Washington Street view of the Empire State framed by the arches.

name: Williamsburg
short_description: Warehouse blocks turned to music venues, vintage shops and waterfront bars, with the L train straight in from Manhattan.

name: Bushwick
short_description: Industrial streets covered in commissioned murals around the Bushwick Collective, with galleries in the old lofts.

name: Red Hook
short_description: A cut-off waterfront neighborhood of cobbles and warehouses, with harbour views and no subway of its own.

name: Park Slope
short_description: Brownstone blocks on the slope below Prospect Park, with Fifth Avenue shopping and a strong food street on Seventh.

name: Coney Island
short_description: The original seaside amusement district, with the Cyclone, the Wonder Wheel and Nathan's on Surf Avenue.

name: Smorgasburg
short_description: An open-air food market of around a hundred vendors, running weekends from spring through autumn on the waterfront.

name: Brooklyn Flea
short_description: Weekend stalls of antiques, vintage clothing and salvage, held under the Manhattan Bridge archway in DUMBO.

name: DeKalb Market Hall
short_description: Forty vendors underground in Downtown Brooklyn, including an outpost of the original Katz's pastrami counter.

name: Industry City
short_description: Six million square feet of converted Sunset Park warehouses holding food halls, makers and design studios.

name: Brooklyn Academy of Music
short_description: America's oldest operating performing arts centre, programming opera, dance and the Next Wave festival.

name: St. Ann's Warehouse
short_description: Experimental theatre in a converted tobacco warehouse, with a walled garden open to the public beside it.

name: Kings Theatre
short_description: A 1929 Loew's Wonder Theatre in Flatbush, restored to its full gilded interior and booking touring acts.

name: Barclays Center
short_description: The weathered-steel arena at Atlantic Terminal, home to the Nets and a regular concert stop.

name: Pioneer Works
short_description: A Red Hook ironworks turned arts and science centre, with a triple height main hall and a free garden.

name: Prospect Park Bandshell
short_description: The outdoor stage that hosts the free BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn summer concert season inside Prospect Park.

name: Coney Island Boardwalk
short_description: Two and a half miles of boardwalk along the Atlantic, running from Sea Gate past the aquarium to Brighton Beach.

name: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge
short_description: The double-deck suspension span across the Narrows to Staten Island, and the starting line of the city marathon.

name: MoMA PS1
address: Long Island City, New York, NY
short_description: MoMA's contemporary wing in a former Long Island City schoolhouse, with the Warm Up music series in the courtyard.

name: Museum of the Moving Image
short_description: Film, television and video game history on the Astoria studio lot, including a Jim Henson gallery.

name: Queens Museum
short_description: Home to the Panorama of the City of New York, a 9,335 square foot scale model built for the 1964 World's Fair.

name: New York Hall of Science
short_description: A hands-on science museum in a 1964 World's Fair pavilion, with a large outdoor science playground.

name: The Noguchi Museum
address: Long Island City, New York, NY
short_description: Isamu Noguchi's own museum and sculpture garden, arranged across a converted photo-engraving plant.

name: Socrates Sculpture Park
short_description: A former landfill turned open-air studio and exhibition space on the East River, free and open every day.

name: Flushing Meadows Corona Park
short_description: The 1939 and 1964 World's Fair grounds, now the borough's largest park, holding the Unisphere and two museums.

name: Gantry Plaza State Park
address: Long Island City, New York, NY
short_description: Restored rail gantries on the Long Island City waterfront, with piers facing the midtown skyline across the river.

name: Astoria Park
short_description: Sloping lawns between the Triborough and Hell Gate bridges, with the largest and oldest public pool in the city.

name: Forest Park
short_description: 538 acres over a glacial moraine, holding one of the last continuous oak forests left in Queens.

name: Queens Botanical Garden
short_description: Thirty-nine acres built around a rose garden and a wedding garden, with a LEED-platinum visitor centre.

name: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge
short_description: A federal refuge inside the city limits, on the Atlantic flyway, where over three hundred bird species have been recorded.

name: Louis Armstrong House Museum
short_description: The Corona house Armstrong lived in from 1943 until his death, kept with its original interiors and tape archive.

name: Bowne House
short_description: A 1661 Quaker farmhouse tied to the Flushing Remonstrance, an early American argument for religious liberty.

name: King Manor Museum
short_description: The Jamaica home of Rufus King, a signer of the Constitution and an early campaigner against slavery.

name: Unisphere
short_description: The twelve-storey stainless steel globe built as the theme symbol of the 1964 World's Fair, ringed by fountains.

name: New York State Pavilion
short_description: Philip Johnson's ruined World's Fair pavilion, its Tent of Tomorrow towers still standing over the park.

name: Astoria
short_description: A long-standing Greek neighborhood now layered with Egyptian, Bangladeshi and Balkan food along Steinway Street.

name: Jackson Heights
short_description: Garden apartment blocks and one of the most linguistically diverse square miles on earth, along Roosevelt Avenue.

name: Flushing Chinatown
short_description: The largest Chinatown outside Manhattan, centred on Main Street, with regional food courts in the basements.

name: Rockaway Beach
short_description: Seven miles of Atlantic surf beach reachable by subway, with the only legal surfing breaks in the city.

name: Hunter's Point South Park
address: Long Island City, New York, NY
short_description: A resilient waterfront park of salt marsh and lawn, designed to flood, facing the United Nations across the river.

name: Queens Night Market
short_description: A Saturday evening market behind the Hall of Science, with scores of vendors capped at low fixed prices.

name: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center
short_description: The largest public tennis facility in the world and the site of the US Open every summer.

name: SculptureCenter
address: Long Island City, New York, NY
short_description: A Maya Lin-renovated trolley repair shop in Long Island City, showing emerging sculptors in raw industrial rooms.

name: Bronx Museum of the Arts
short_description: Contemporary art on the Grand Concourse with a focus on Bronx artists, free to enter every day it opens.

name: Wave Hill
short_description: A public garden and estate above the Hudson, with a pergola looking across to the New Jersey Palisades.

name: New York Botanical Garden
short_description: 250 acres holding a Victorian glasshouse, a fifty-acre old-growth forest and the country's largest herbarium.

name: Bronx Zoo
short_description: The largest metropolitan zoo in the country, with the Congo Gorilla Forest and a monorail through Wild Asia.

name: Van Cortlandt Park
address: Van Cortlandt Village, New York, NY
short_description: Over a thousand acres of forest, freshwater lake and the oldest public golf course in the United States.

name: Pelham Bay Park
short_description: The city's largest park at three times the size of Central Park, with salt marsh, woodland and a public beach.

name: Bronx Documentary Center
short_description: A nonprofit gallery in Melrose showing documentary photography and running free classes for local students.

name: Edgar Allan Poe Cottage
short_description: The small wooden cottage where Poe spent his last years and wrote Annabel Lee, kept in Poe Park.

name: Bartow-Pell Mansion Museum
short_description: An 1842 Greek Revival country house in Pelham Bay Park, with a walled terrace garden running down to the sound.

name: Woodlawn Cemetery
short_description: A National Historic Landmark burial ground where Duke Ellington, Miles Davis and Herman Melville are buried.

name: Yankee Stadium
short_description: The 2009 stadium beside the original site, with Monument Park behind centre field honouring retired numbers.

name: Orchard Beach
short_description: A mile-long crescent of sand built by Robert Moses in Pelham Bay Park, with a colonnaded bathhouse behind it.

name: City Island
short_description: A former shipbuilding village a mile and a half long, reached by one bridge and lined with seafood houses.

name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
short_description: An indoor market built in 1940 at the centre of the Belmont Italian quarter, with butchers, bakers and cheese stalls.

name: The High Bridge
short_description: The oldest surviving bridge in the city, an 1848 aqueduct span reopened as a footpath over the Harlem River.

name: Staten Island Museum
short_description: The borough's museum of art, natural history and archives, now housed in a restored building at Snug Harbor.

name: National Lighthouse Museum
short_description: On the site of the former Lighthouse Depot at St George, telling the story of American lighthouse keeping.

name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
short_description: Eighty-three acres of Greek Revival buildings and botanical gardens, including a walled Chinese scholar's garden.

name: Staten Island Greenbelt
short_description: Two thousand eight hundred acres of connected woodland and wetland, with thirty-five miles of marked trail.

name: Conference House Park
short_description: The southernmost point of New York State, with a 1680 manor house where a failed 1776 peace conference was held.

name: Alice Austen House
short_description: The waterfront cottage of a pioneering woman photographer, looking across the Narrows to Brooklyn.

name: Fort Wadsworth
short_description: One of the oldest military sites in the country, under the Verrazzano approach, with batteries open to walk through.

name: St. George
short_description: The ferry landing neighborhood, with a ballpark, a courthouse district and the best free harbour view in the city.

name: South Beach
short_description: Two and a half miles of Atlantic boardwalk named for FDR, facing Brooklyn across the Lower Bay.

name: Staten Island Ferry
short_description: A free twenty-five minute crossing running around the clock, passing close by the Statue of Liberty each way.
